beats.intent: ThinkSR runs the image through encoding, windowing, shared DQ-CTM ticks, and decoding, with recurrence inside the thought stage.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: The method keeps a dense carrier while a compact process reads and updates it. The encoder turns the low-resolution input into features. Windowing prepares the dense field for local processing. DQ-CTM runs shared ticks, so the same parameters recur inside the thought process. The decoder turns the updated features back into the super-resolved image.

params.headline: ThinkSR keeps recurrence inside the thought stage
params.note: The loop returns to DQ-CTM, not to the whole flow.

beats.intent: The carrier starts as encoder features from the low-resolution image, and window partitioning keeps all tokens in the dense field.
beats.narration: The carrier equation defines the dense state that the method preserves. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into the feature field. The window operator partitions that feature field without dropping tokens.

params.headline: The dense carrier is encoded, then windowed

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the comparison; at 1.129 million parameters, it is second largest of the five.
beats.claim: Table 1 — ×4 lightweight super-resolution, average over five benchmarks.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison puts the lightweight methods in size order. CATANet is the smallest at zero point five three five million parameters. RFDN and IMDN are still below one million parameters. DQ-CTM-SR has one point one two nine million parameters, making it the second largest of the five. CARN is larger, at one point five nine two million parameters.
